kept.title: Insecure CI configuration disables SSL verification
kept.description: The CI workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml explicitly disables SSL verification for Node 0.x via `npm config set strict-ssl false`, exposing the supply chain to man-in-the-middle attacks.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attack on the CI network traffic
Intercept requests to the npm registry
Inject malicious code into the dependencies fetched during the build
CI pipeline will trust and execute the malicious package
kept.impact: CI/CD environment compromise, allowing injection of backdoors into the published package.

kept.title: Unsafe child process execution in benchmark runner
kept.description: benchmark/index.js uses `spawn` with unsanitized file names fetched from the filesystem, which could lead to command injection if malicious files are present in the directory.
steps_to_exploit: Place a file with a malicious name (e.g., shell commands) into the benchmark folder
Wait for the benchmark script to run
The script triggers the file via `spawn(exe, [fullPath])`, potentially executing shell sequences
kept.impact: Arbitrary command execution in the development environment.

kept.title: Potential prototype pollution via IP_RANGES lookup
kept.description: The code uses `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call` correctly but the `IP_RANGES` object is mutable and could be polluted if the environment is shared.
steps_to_exploit: Exploit a separate vulnerability to pollute the global Object prototype
The logic in `compile` may then incorrectly access or modify the hardcoded `IP_RANGES` map
Modify the range values to bypass security checks in `trust`
kept.impact: Security logic bypass by manipulating internal trust configurations.

kept.title: Insecure use of `apply` for argument injection
kept.description: In `index.js`, the code uses `trust.splice.apply(trust, [i, 1].concat(val))` to insert subnets. If `val` (from `IP_RANGES`) contains unexpected data, it could lead to stack overflows or logic errors.
steps_to_exploit: Target an environment where `IP_RANGES` can be modified
Inject a massive array of values into `IP_RANGES`
Trigger the `compile` function, causing the `apply` operation to exceed stack limits or cause denial of service

kept.title: Potential integer overflow in parseipNotation
kept.description: The range parsing logic converts substrings to integers using `parseInt(range, 10)` without strict bounds checking until after conversion, potentially allowing negative or extremely large values.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a specially crafted IP string with a high range value
The `parseInt` logic processes it, potentially hitting edge cases in logic validation
Trigger errors in `parseipNotation` or bypass validation checks
kept.impact: Logic error leading to misconfigured IP trust ranges.

kept.title: Dependency on vulnerable version of ipaddr.js
kept.description: The package uses `ipaddr.js` version 1.9.1, which has had known issues with regex-based IP parsing that could lead to ReDoS in certain contexts.
steps_to_exploit: Identify an input vector that reaches `ipaddr.js` parsing logic
Send a long, complex, or specifically crafted malicious IP address string
Observe high CPU usage in the Node.js event loop

kept.title: Unsafe handling of untrusted input in parseipNotation
kept.description: The function `parseipNotation` concatenates raw input `str` directly into an error message, which is then thrown. This could lead to information disclosure or log poisoning.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a malicious crafted string as an IP argument
Trigger the `TypeError`
Observe the stack trace and error message in server logs
Potentially extract internal file paths or server-side state

kept.title: Use of `npm rm --save-dev` on CI might break build parity
kept.description: The CI workflow dynamically removes development dependencies, which can lead to unpredictable builds that do not match local development environments.
steps_to_exploit: The CI environment modifies its own dependency tree dynamically
A developer might be testing with local plugins that the CI pipeline explicitly removes
Security vulnerabilities or bugs are masked in the production build
kept.impact: Loss of build consistency and potential security regression.

kept.title: Lack of input sanitization for X-Forwarded-For header
kept.description: The library relies on `forwarded` package to parse `X-Forwarded-For` without performing strict validation on the headers provided by the client, trusting proxy headers blindly.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a request with spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` headers
The library parses these headers to determine the client IP
An attacker bypasses IP-based access control or rate limiting
kept.impact: Access control bypass and security policy enforcement failure.

kept.title: Insecure use of `apply` in `trustMulti`
kept.description: Similar to the compilation step, the `trust` logic performs complex array operations that are opaque and could be prone to resource exhaustion if the input is highly manipulated.
steps_to_exploit: Define an excessively large trust array
Execute the `trust` function on many incoming requests
Consume memory resources on the Node.js process

kept.title: Implicitly trusting all forwarded addresses
kept.description: If `trust` is not provided to `proxyaddr`, it defaults to returning all addresses, which might be misused by developers as a source of truth for security decisions.
steps_to_exploit: Developer uses `proxyaddr(req)` without a trust function
The application trusts the last element of the list as the client IP
The attacker provides a forged `X-Forwarded-For` chain
Application grants permissions based on the forged IP

kept.title: Potential ReDoS in IP notation string parsing
kept.description: The logic performs string manipulation and regex testing using `DIGIT_REGEXP` on user-provided strings for range identification.
steps_to_exploit: Supply an extremely long string for the 'range' part of an IP notation
The regex engine processes the input, potentially leading to excessive CPU usage during evaluation
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via regex complexity.

kept.title: Outdated development dependencies in package.json
kept.description: Many devDependencies (e.g., mocha 8.4.0) have known vulnerabilities that, while not affecting production, could compromise the security of the build server.
steps_to_exploit: Target the development machine or build server
Use an exploit directed at a specific vulnerable version of one of the devDependencies
Gain access to the source code repository or build environment

kept.title: Use of shell expansion in CI environment
kept.description: The script uses bash expansion and pipes in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that could be influenced by environment variables or manipulated files in the repo.
steps_to_exploit: Modify a local config file or environment variable recognized by the CI environment
The bash script `npm config get package-lock` interprets the shell input
Execute unauthorized code during the build process

kept.title: Reliance on `process.cwd()` in benchmark tool
kept.description: The benchmark script uses `process.cwd()` to resolve paths, which can be inconsistent if the script is executed from different locations, leading to accidental execution of wrong scripts.
steps_to_exploit: Navigate to a different directory
Run the benchmark from there
The tool might resolve paths relative to the current working directory instead of the intended benchmark directory
Execute local scripts with potentially harmful content
